name: German nationalism
summary: German nationalism holds that the Germans form one nation defined by language, culture and shared history, and that it should have a unified state of its own. It arose in the Napoleonic era, drove the 1848 Frankfurt Parliament and the unification of 1871, and in Imperial Germany shifted toward an authoritarian, militarist and expansionist form. It has little to say on welfare or social policy, but backs protection of national industry, strong armed forces and national cultural unity.
scope: The national movement from Herder, Fichte, Arndt and Jahn through the Vormarz, the 1848 Frankfurt Parliament and Bismarckian unification, with the Wilhelmine Pan-German strand as its later form. It excludes Nazism, which is a separate racial ideology, and post-1945 patriotism. Economic and social answers are mostly low-confidence inferences, as the movement was a constitutional and cultural project.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The national movement of 1806-1871 had no health policy; Imperial Germany later built state insurance but nationalists did not frame it as a core demand, so this is a weak inference.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Minimum wages are anachronistic for a movement of liberal burghers and conservative nationalists who prized economic development over wage regulation; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: List attacked pure free-market cosmopolitanism for developing nations yet nationalist liberals backed commerce and property, so adherents were split.

public-ownership.rationale: List promoted state-backed railways as a national unifier, but nationalists did not call for public ownership of industry generally; inferred and split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The bourgeois and conservative base of the movement did not campaign for steeper taxes on the wealthy; inferred from its class makeup.

unions-good.rationale: Imperial-era nationalism was anti-socialist and authoritarian, treating class organisation as divisive to the Volksgemeinschaft; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Liberal nationalists at Frankfurt wrote property protections into a bill of basic rights, and the movement was bourgeois, though not absolute.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Nationalists wanted economic strength under national direction, but corporate regulation as such was not a theme; no clear stance.

cut-welfare.rationale: Welfare politics were not a nationalist issue; the Imperial strand accepted state social insurance as a bond to the nation, so cutting it is not typical.

worker-ownership.rationale: Worker ownership belongs to socialist currents that the Imperial nationalism opposed as anti-national; inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Imperial nationalism was authoritarian and security-minded, so tolerance of state surveillance against internal enemies is a reasonable inference.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Moral-order and national-vitality themes (Jahn's gymnastics) point against recreational drug use, though the issue was never addressed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The movement valued free speech against absolutism (Jahn, Frankfurt rights), and its own rhetoric against Poles, Jews and French would not have been restricted.

strong-leader.rationale: Liberal nationalists wanted a parliamentary monarchy while the Bismarckian strand welcomed strong Prussian leadership, so the movement was divided.

state-harmful.rationale: Fichte called the state a means to the nation's development, and the movement's whole aim was to build a unified state.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control was not an issue; the movement valued citizen-soldiers but no clear stance on private ownership.

empower-police-military.rationale: Pan-German and Imperial nationalists backed a strong army and navy, and the national movement was tied to military pride.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Jahn-style moral regeneration through discipline suggests disapproval, but the issue was not addressed; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: The movement sought a centralised national state to overcome particularism of the many German states, though federal compromises existed.

rehabilitation.rationale: Penal philosophy was not a nationalist theme; adherents were split between reform and retribution.

traditional-family.rationale: Jahn's Volkstum and Imperial nationalism upheld the patriarchal family as the basis of the national community.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Entirely anachronistic; a conservative-national movement of the period would have rejected it, inferred from its moral outlook.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; national vitality and moral-order concerns point to opposition, but this is an inference.

more-religion-public.rationale: Protestant cultural dominance marked the Imperial strand while Fichte and liberals favoured freedom of conscience, so adherents split.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's racialised hierarchy (Arndt on Poles and Slavs) points against redress programs.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The movement held fixed sex roles in the national community; inferred since the idea is anachronistic.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Fichte and Jahn made defending German language, culture and spirit against foreign influence the core of the movement.

gradual-change.rationale: The national movement sought to overturn the order of princely states and press for unification, though some strands accepted evolution under Prussia.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration was not a 19th-century issue, but Weimar-era nationalism aimed to exclude immigrants and the modern strand (AfD) favours cuts.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The movement prized national independence; Fichte feared even a benevolent foreign power cannot grasp German well-being.

free-trade.rationale: List argued free trade suits only advanced nations and called for protection of German industry.

nation-first.rationale: Fichte placed the nation's continuity above the individual and wary of foreign influence; the nation's interest was the highest political aim.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The movement concerned itself with national power rather than universal human rights abroad; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Fichte and Arndt treated the nation as a bounded cultural community, so open borders contradict its premise.

limit-growth.rationale: List and the Zollverein tradition pursued industrial growth as national strength; limiting it was not on the agenda.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: List championed railways and industry as national progress, but romantic nationalists distrusted modernity, so mixed.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic; no stance can be derived beyond a general wish for national self-sufficiency.

revolution-justified.rationale: The 1848 liberals and Jahn's circle pursued national unity by revolutionary means, while Bismarckian and conservative nationalists rejected revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: The Frankfurt 'Professors' Parliament' was elite-led yet popular sovereignty was a stated aim; split.

central-planning.rationale: List favoured state guidance of development stages but within market economies; full planning is not nationalist doctrine.

socialized-markets.rationale: Market socialism is socialist doctrine opposed by Imperial nationalism; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Property-owning bourgeois and aristocratic supporters would resist heavy inheritance tax; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Anachronistic and at odds with a work-and-duty national ethos; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: List's national system made protective tariffs for German industry a central economic demand of the national movement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: List argued the state should steer economic development through tariffs, railways and legislation to build national productive power.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Romantic nationalists praised peasantry and Mittelstand, but the movement also served industrial burghers; no clear stance.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Imperial nationalism was anti-socialist and bourgeois, rejecting abolition of wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: List's state-guided national economy favours national monetary institutions; inferred.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Volksgemeinschaft ideas pointed toward class harmony, but state-run wage bodies were not a stated demand of the earlier movement.

one-party-rule.rationale: The Frankfurt liberal strand wanted parliamentary government with parties; one-party rule is Nazi-era, which this profile excludes.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Frankfurt offered a hereditary emperor and Bismarck unified under the Prussian crown; Jahn wanted a Hohenzollern monarchy.

democracy-best.rationale: The liberal-democratic wing of 1848 backed popular sovereignty while the Bismarckian strand was authoritarian, so the movement split.

direct-votes.rationale: The Frankfurt approach was representative parliament; direct legislation was not a theme.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils belong to the socialist left that German nationalism opposed as anti-national.

right-to-secede.rationale: A movement seeking a unified nation-state sought to prevent fragmentation of Germans, though it championed its own self-determination.

natural-rulers.rationale: Imperial nationalism accepted aristocratic leadership but liberals stressed equality before the law; split.

political-violence-never.rationale: Jahn's Lützow Free Corps and the 1848 barricades show acceptance of violence for the national cause.

war-builds-character.rationale: Pan-German and Imperial nationalists glorified war and Fichte justified sacrifice for the nation; Jahn trained youth for national struggle.

separate-church-state.rationale: Frankfurt liberals favoured freedom of religion but the Imperial strand backed Protestant dominance and the Kulturkampf; split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The movement based law on nation and constitution rather than scripture, though it had Protestant colouring.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Fichte treated the state as the instrument of the nation, and national defence as a public duty.

military-superiority.rationale: The Pan-German League and Wilhelmine nationalists pursued German military and naval power against rivals.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Fichte's Volk is defined by language and culture; Arndt pictured ethnic homogeneity, though the movement also sought Germans of many states.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Imperial nationalism opposed socialism and offered the Volksgemeinschaft as an alternative to class conflict.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not part of a nationalist-bourgeois program; the movement opposed socialist leveling.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Pan-German expansion into Central and Eastern Europe disregarded other peoples' claims; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: German colonialism was justified as civilising mission; adherents would deny reparation claims.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalists favoured union of German speakers (Greater Germany), but not of broader civilizations or religions.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Fichte subordinated the individual to the nation's eternal life, rejecting self-interest as the moral basis.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Fichte demanded sacrifice for the nation, and Imperial nationalism stressed duty to the national community.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Romanticism valued nature but the movement had no environmental doctrine.

limit-population.rationale: Lebensraum and national-strength thinking favour growing population; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: List and the Zollverein tradition embraced industrialisation, though romantics were sceptical.

accelerate-technology.rationale: List championed technological modernisation like railways, but disruption of institutions was not welcome.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; Jahn's physical-regeneration culture was collective and traditional.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from preference for human national leadership.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis for a position.

restore-past-order.rationale: Romantic nationalists idealised medieval German history (Arndt) yet the movement aimed at a new national state; split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Fichte and Arndt insisted on the nation's spiritual mission, not pragmatic evaluation; inferred.

direct-action.rationale: Jahn's gymnasts and Burschenschaften used mass action while Frankfurt relied on parliament; split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Nationalists promoted industry and railways as national power; foraging is far from their aims.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: List's developmental theory depends on manufacturing and specialisation.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A socialist principle opposed by Imperial nationalism.

production-for-use.rationale: Socialist slogan; nationalists backed profit-driven but nationally directed production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: A Marxist claim rejected by nationalists who denied class antagonism.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Imperial nationalism was anti-socialist and anti-communist.

collective-farming.rationale: Arndt celebrated free peasant proprietors and the nationalists opposed collectivisation.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist thesis; nationalists attributed wars to national rivalry rather than capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: List and the movement wanted a taxing and tariff-levying national state for development and defence.

harm-principle.rationale: The Frankfurt liberals wrote basic rights, but nationalists also demanded moral conformity; split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Fichte and Jahn gave the nation priority over the individual, though liberals protected individual rights.

conscription.rationale: Jahn's Lützow Corps and the Prussian reforms made universal national service an ideal of the citizen-nation.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Fichte's ideal binds individual life to the nation; leaving as the main check is opposed.

state-as-business.rationale: Fichte saw the state as the national community's instrument, not a firm with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Fichte's freedom as staying German in spirit resembles a positive notion, but not material means; unclear.

media-academia-power.rationale: The 'Professors' Parliament' valued academics' role, but no doctrine on this claim.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Imperial-era racial and Social Darwinist currents entered nationalism, though the earlier movement defined the nation by culture; contested.

organic-representation.rationale: Romantic corporate representation appealed to some conservatives, while Frankfurt favoured parliamentary parties; split.

total-state.rationale: The liberal nationalist mainstream wanted limited constitutional government; total state is Nazi-era.

national-rebirth.rationale: Fichte's addresses and Jahn's movement aimed at spiritual and physical rebirth of a humiliated nation after 1806.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Pan-Germanism and Wilhelmine nationalists demanded expansion and hegemony in Central and Eastern Europe.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The national movement stood for constitutional nation-state rather than feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Arndt campaigned against serfdom in Pomerania and Rugen.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Fichte's idealism is not the postmodern thesis; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Fichte held a universal outlook as the goal but grounded it in German particularity; split.

single-common-good.rationale: Fichte and Imperial nationalism stressed the unified national interest (Volksgemeinschaft) over class interest.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Nationalism of the period was hostile to Jews as Germany's misfortune (Jahn), and no endorsement is documented.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Weimar-era heredity citizenship law was designed to include emigrant Germans and ethnic Germans abroad.

revive-national-language.rationale: German was already living language; Fichte urged cultural purity, but revival of a lapsed language is not applicable.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Nationalists opposed socialist workplace control as divisive of the national community.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education policy under Fichte meant a national state-run education to form the national spirit, but voucher markets did not exist; no clear stance.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Modern fiscal debate with no counterpart in the 1806-1871 movement; adherents have no documented position.

economic-freedom.rationale: Liberal nationalists coupled political and economic freedom but List's wing rejected laissez-faire; split.

rule-by-example.rationale: Fichte put education and a state organised around the nation, not moral exemplarity alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament's aim was a German nation-state, and self-determination was the movement's founding claim.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; nationalism's priority of national interest favours willingness to use force unilaterally.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Fichte's idealism and Romanticism valued both reason and spirit; split.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Weimar-era citizenship law aimed to exclude immigrants from the Volk; inferred for welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Duty-and-work national ethos suggests support; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Volksgemeinschaft ideology offered national solidarity over class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Defence of inherited German culture and memory is core.

dominated-front.rationale: Anachronistic; German nationalism did not seek alliance of dominated countries.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalists insisted workers belong to the nation first, rejecting international class solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Jahn and Imperial nationalism upheld distinct roles for men and women in the national community.

ban-interest.rationale: Antisemitic tropes about usury existed but the nationalist mainstream backed commerce; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Segregation by law was Nazi-era (Nuremberg), outside this scope.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist thesis rejected by nationalists who saw the state as embodiment of the nation.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Coal powered the industrial growth List and the Zollverein championed, but oil and gas policy is anachronistic; no firm stance.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Nationalists demanded cultural conformity; Weimar-era law aimed to exclude immigrants, assimilation inferred.

elite-replacement.rationale: A recent far-right conspiracy theory, not documented in the historical movement.

proportional-representation.rationale: Frankfurt electoral law and later movement had no clear stance.

national-mission.rationale: Fichte saw Germans as an original people with a mission for humanity, giving the nation a special calling.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The nationalist movement upheld male-led institutions and did not recognise systemic advantage as a problem.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics entered later; not defining of the mainstream strand.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nationalism defended the army and police; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: List called for state-led development and the movement for a strong unified state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Culture-based nationhood did not center on race early on; later racialism split.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Arndt held Poles and Slavs inferior, contradicting equal worth, though liberals backed equality before law.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Eastward expansion thinking and colonial empire show nationalists did not view settlement as colonial wrong.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: National unification needed a common legal order; Frankfurt aimed at uniform rights.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; Los von Rom campaigned to convert Catholics so conversion was not opposed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Split between liberal secularism and Protestant cultural dominance.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The 1848 liberal nationalists grounded the state in popular sovereignty and national consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: List's protectionist national economics and mercantilist strand favour export strength.

population-transfer.rationale: Pan-Germanists pushed expansion and Germanisation but explicit transfer was Nazi-era; split.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Nationalists fought wars of unification and expansion (Bismarck, Pan-Germans).

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Social Darwinist currents in Imperial nationalism described struggle between peoples as progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Not addressed in the period; split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Fichte's freedom from foreign domination resembles this but applied to nations; ambiguous.

separated-powers.rationale: The Frankfurt constitution created an emperor, parliament and judiciary with checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Leninist idea rejected by anti-socialist nationalists.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a 20th-century British policy with no counterpart in the movement; no documented position.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Imperial nationalists were anti-socialist and favoured restricting labor militancy.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Nationalists blamed foreign rule and disunity rather than population for weakness, but no stated doctrine exists on poverty causes.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Arndt's picture of ethnic homogeneity and Imperial Protestant cultural dominance saw diversity as a threat to national unity.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Frankfurt used elections; lottery is alien.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Imperial authoritarian strand accepted emergency measures against internal enemies like socialists and Catholics.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price fixing was not a nationalist theme, and List's tariff economics did not address it; split and inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Nationalists fought censorship (Jahn demanded free speech) so media control by party is opposed.

party-commands-army.rationale: Imperial army answered to the crown, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Weimar-era law of descent and nationalist ethos favoured exclusion of immigrants.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Parliamentarians were educated bourgeois; no wage-equalisation stance.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Postwar collaborative nationalism embedded Germany in Europe, but the historical movement prized national sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Frankfurt and Imperial constitutions gave the emperor command and ministerial choice.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Protestant national tradition lacks bishops-led governance.

clerical-rule.rationale: Kulturkampf and anti-Catholic Imperial nationalism rejected clerical political power.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A revolutionary-socialist stance against which national loyalty was defined.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Jahn's moral concerns versus free-speech aims; split.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Frankfurt scheme had a hereditary emperor, so presidential term limits were not discussed; no position.

recall-officials.rationale: Recall of officials was not part of the Frankfurt constitutional design, and the movement never addressed it.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Wilhelmine nationalists wanted strong alliances and power rather than retreat.

people-in-arms.rationale: Jahn's Lützow Free Corps and the Landwehr ideal of the nation in arms.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Arndt's romanticised peasant community and later Volk ideology idealised rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Unification of divided German states was the movement's central goal, and Greater German union with Austria was long its demand.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Nationalists were themselves the educated; no stance.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Arndt held Germans pure and Slavs inferior, and Fichte treated Germans as an original people.

death-penalty.rationale: Imperial authoritarian strand supported capital punishment.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral regeneration themes suggest support; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Weimar and earlier law defined the Volk by heredity, and the tradition kept descent-based citizenship for a century.

minority-language-support.rationale: Imperial Germany pushed Germanisation of Poles and Danes.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The Kulturkampf and national uniformity ethos opposed special treatment.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Nationalism demanded conformity to a national spirit.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Anachronistic; Germans were strict on debts as in Greek crisis.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: List linked political and economic independence yet not to property transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament was an elected national assembly to write the constitution.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Imperial authoritarian modernisation versus liberal rights; split.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nationalism puts national interest first, so global aid is not a duty; inferred.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Frankfurt chose hereditary emperor; no direct election stance.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking was outside the movement's agenda, though List wanted national control of economic policy; no clear stance.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Pan-German and Weimar-era nationalism refused loss of German land, as in resentment of Versailles.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Not clearly stated; split between liberal property rights and national solidarity.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is a modern concern with no basis in the nationalist canon; no position can be derived.

collective-defense.rationale: Imperial nationalists favoured alliances like the Triple Alliance; mutual defence inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Pan-German annexation aims show nationalists did not hold this.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Kulturkampf was a national-liberal and Bismarckian effort to curb Catholic Church power.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The emperor in the Frankfurt scheme stood above parties as a national symbol.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: A nation-state project defended unity by force (e.g. Prussian wars of unification).

region-keeps-system.rationale: National unification aimed at uniform law, though federal state structures remained.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The movement's constitutional-monarchy form rejected divine-descent claims.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Income tax design was not discussed by the national movement, and Imperial Germany used progressive state taxes; no firm stance.

character-from-environment.rationale: Fichte's national character as inborn spirit, not environment.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Frankfurt liberals wanted constitutional limits on rulers.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; Pan-German ambitions were territorial in Europe, so nothing can be said beyond a general love of national greatness.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Frankfurt mixed monarchy with parliament, but not a theory of the few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Bismarck cult existed in the Empire, but the liberal movement was against it; split.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law was not a nationalist issue, and traditional family ideals do not settle the question; no documented position.

land-redistribution.rationale: Arndt backed peasant freedom but the movement was property-protecting.

refugee-return.rationale: Pan-Germans championed ethnic Germans' rights abroad; return of expelled Germans is a postwar concern, inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Pan-Germanism claimed Greater Germany for all German speakers, a central demand.

common-currency.rationale: List's Zollverein pushed economic union; modern collaborative nationalism accepted euro; split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Pan-Germanism sought union of Germanic peoples across borders.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Imperial Germany Germanised minorities instead of granting them autonomy.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Fichte's idealism and nationalism stress spirit and culture over economic base.

ban-cartels.rationale: List's nationalism backed strong national industry; cartels were permitted in the Empire.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bank rescues were not on the movement's agenda; List's state-guided economics might allow them while bourgeois liberals would not.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Liberal nationalists wanted rights; populist nationalists want majority power; split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Alien to traditional gender roles of the movement.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: List supported protection but not full autarky; Pan-Germans sought self-sufficient bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Modern trade-treaty design had no counterpart; List's protectionism rejects supranational rules, but the topic was never addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Fichte's duty to nation points that way, but not as economic doctrine.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Lützow Free Corps shows armed volunteers; not a doctrine.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Liberals wanted equality before law, but monarchy and Junkers lasted; split.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Fichte and Arndt centred education on German history and spirit.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: German colonialism was justified as civilising mission.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a modern policy not addressed by the movement; its racial hierarchy cuts both ways, so no clear position.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation was not addressed by the national movement, so adherents have no documented position.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Nationalists believed in industrial capitalism with national organisation, rejecting Marxist collapse.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Pan-German and Wilhelmine nationalism wanted influence in Central Europe once ruled by the Holy Roman Empire, inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: List sought protection for development and later integration.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The movement never addressed private-association rights; its liberals and its exclusionary nationalists would split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament drafted a basic-rights catalogue, and its constitution influenced the Basic Law.

elective-rulers.rationale: Frankfurt offered a hereditary emperor, but liberals wanted parliament; split.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: 1848 liberals took up arms to enforce constitution.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Frankfurt liberals favoured parliament, Bismarckian stream the crown; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics was not part of the nationalist canon, though romantic nature feeling gave some sympathy; no clear position.

animal-use-humane.rationale: The movement left animal use unaddressed, and its rural, agrarian idealisation accepted farming and hunting; no documented stance.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Conservative Imperial elite accepted paternal duties; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Fichte demanded active service to the nation.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Nationalists criticised princely particularism but Imperial strand defended its own elite; no consistent anti-elite stance.

patriotic-education.rationale: Fichte's addresses proposed national education to form a strong national spirit, and Jahn trained youth for the fatherland.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Anachronistic; the national movement used culture and education to build the nation, not as a pacifier. Inferred.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Anachronistic; nationalists stressed authority and national unity rather than a theory of consent. Inferred.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: List saw free trade as favouring dominant Britain, but no nationalist theory of surplus transfer; inferred and split.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from the heredity-based, ethnic idea of the nation.

party-own-road.rationale: Inferred from the stress on national self-determination and rejection of foreign direction.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from List's national economy and protection to build national industry.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Pan-German and Wilhelmine nationalism pursued Greater Germany and recovery of German-populated lands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the ethnic nation: the culturally German hold political leadership in the state.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement predates fascism and is inferred to give it no constitutional role.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anachronistic; the historic movement did not face the question, adherents split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Anachronistic and outside the movement's concerns.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from the movement's cult of national memory and monuments.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal social order of the movement.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from Fichte's idea that each nation develops its own character and institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from the army's central role in Imperial Germany and nationalist support for strong armed forces.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from traditional family and gender roles in the movement.

filial-duty.rationale: Fichte and Jahn stressed family and communal duty in national upbringing, but the point is not a central nationalist demand; inferred.

office-by-exam.rationale: The movement was a constitutional and cultural project; Frankfurt delegates were split between merit and class-based officeholding.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Friedrich List's national economics supported protecting national industry, which suggests shielding strategic firms; inferred.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The movement upheld traditional marriage and family and its Wilhelmine form was socially conservative; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament was a representative body with free mandates and nationalists opposed binding imperative mandates; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: List's national system and Imperial Germany's state insurance point to state rather than private-account pensions; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Nationalists accepted private property and landholding; inferred from the constitutional liberal and conservative strands.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Budget approval by parliament was a central liberal demand of 1848 and the Frankfurt constitution gave the parliament that power.

single-official-language.rationale: Fichte and Arndt tied nation to the German language, and Imperial Germany promoted German in schooling at the expense of Polish and other languages.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The movement had no doctrine on foreign land ownership; adherents' views are not documented.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The concept is anachronistic and the movement's ethnic-national outlook would not favour outcome-based anti-discrimination tests; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Jahn's gymnastics movement and Arndt praised simple, hardy living against French luxury and fashion; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The movement had no doctrine on arming foreign insurgents; Pan-Germans favoured pressure on neighbours but not clearly this.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Pan-German and Imperial nationalists backed forcible action to keep German-speaking states in the nation's orbit; inferred from the expansionist strand.

corporate-influence.rationale: Imperial and national movements backed industrialists and the state, so adherents did not make corporate influence a central worry; inferred.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Fichte and Arndt feared foreign cultural influence, so limits on outside money fit the movement; inferred and anachronistic.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Pan-German writers worried about the German population and its strength; inferred, as no source states a policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents are split.

job-guarantee.rationale: List favoured national industry and a strong state, but the movement did not promise jobs to all; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Nationalists of the Wilhelmine period saw power politics as normal and did not hold that democracy brings peace; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Fichte and the Prussian tradition stress duty to the state and the nation; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Nationalists defended German sovereignty but Pan-Germans also claimed other states' territories; adherents split and the position is inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; no stated position.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Pan-German and later nationalists often blamed minorities, but the 1848 mainstream did not; adherents split.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The movement stressed the family and church-state order as foundations of the nation.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament's constitution protected liberal rights, but the later authoritarian strand kept secrets; split.

local-production.rationale: List favoured protecting national production, but the movement did not call for local production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: Jahn's gymnastics and student associations were organised bodies, and the movement sought a single formal national state.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The movement sought a sovereign unified German state and put the national constitution first; inferred for modern international law.

religious-nation.rationale: Nationhood was defined by language, culture and history, not religion, and the nation included Protestants and Catholics.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: German nationalism asserts the German nation's independence and equality, from Fichte's resistance to French domination to Pan-German claims to leadership, and rejects subordinate tribute; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Unifying many states under one national state implied pooling revenue nationally, which the Zollverein and the Reich did; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The national movement had no view on the line between personal and productive property; its supporters were liberal burghers and conservatives and not socialists.

defeat-communism.rationale: Imperial-era nationalists were strongly anti-socialist and hostile to communist revolution; the movement predates communism but its later Wilhelmine form fits; anachronistic and inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The movement did not address service delivery; Imperial Germany used a mix of providers, but nationalists did not frame it, so it is split.

religion-illusion.rationale: Early nationalists such as Arndt and Jahn were Protestant and tied national spirit to Christian faith, rejecting the view that religion is mere illusion; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: List's national economics held that industrial capitalism was the engine of national progress and power; inferred from his stage theory.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nationalists of the period were conservative or liberal on gender roles and gave no support to the view that equality needs economic transformation; inferred.

socialized-care.rationale: Nationalist ideals centred on the family and national duty, such as Jahn's and Arndt's, so public provision of care was foreign to them; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Fichte, Arndt and Jahn campaigned against French words and for a pure German language, and the later language-purism movement followed.

treaties-binding.rationale: The movement's priority was a sovereign state and national unity, so it saw no standing for treaties with internal nations to bind it; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: The nationalists wanted a unified nation-state, not small communal property units; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: Pan-Germanists and the Wilhelmine state promoted German settlement in Polish regions, to bind them to the nation.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The movement was a project of liberals and conservatives who accepted the market economy and the monarchy, so rejecting both capitalism and communism is not its stance; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Pan-Germanism and Arndt's poem claimed German lands wherever German is spoken, with an appeal to history and culture, but language was the main criterion.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic for a movement of 1806-1871 and excluding Nazism; inferred that the historical record is accepted.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Paragraph 175 criminalised male homosexuality in the Prussian code and in the unified empire; nationalists did not contest it; inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Liberal nationalists of 1848 demanded freedoms, while Bismarckian and Wilhelmine nationalism suppressed socialists, so strands diverge.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The movement was largely a secular cultural project; adherents are split between liberal and conservative-Christian views; inferred.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Wilhelmine Pan-Germans backed colonial expansion for the empire's benefit, while earlier nationalists had little interest; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A religious duty alien to German nationalism; inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Nationalists held legitimacy to rest on the nation and constitution, not religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament favoured representative constitutional government, not direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: An anachronistic modern framework opposed to the nationalist emphasis on unity; inferred.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's conservative gender norms, such as Jahn's Turnbewegung ideals.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Christian and conservative norms of the period.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The movement spanned liberal and conservative strands and did not frame its aim this way; split.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marx's thesis was opposed by nationalists who stressed national solidarity over class; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Fichte and Arndt defined the nation by German culture and Christian tradition; inferred, since Islam was not a live issue.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Conservative nationalists upheld monarchy by divine right while 1848 liberals grounded authority in popular sovereignty; split.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed by the movement; adherents are split.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern labour-law detail outside the movement.

social-market-economy.rationale: List's national economics favoured protection of industry, and the term 'social market' is anachronistic; inferred and split.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Jahn, Arndt and Fichte called for national armament, and the Wars of Liberation and Bismarck's unification relied on armed force.

rich-first.rationale: List's infant-industry protection builds national industry for the whole nation, not unequal staged growth; no direct view.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The movement sought German power, and Wilhelmine Pan-Germans sought alliances and expansion; inferred.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament of 1848 offered a hereditary imperial crown, and Imperial Germany was a hereditary monarchy, so inheritance of the head of state was accepted.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Nationalists like List favoured state direction of development and ordinary commercial finance, not user-owned interest-free banks; inferred.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The statement is anachronistic for a movement of 1806-1871; sovereignty favours refusal but national creditworthiness pulls the other way.

property-franchise.rationale: Liberal nationalists at Frankfurt chose a broad male franchise, while Imperial and Prussian nationalists used class franchises, so adherents are split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: The movement held to conventional gender roles and has no ecological doctrine of this kind; inferred.

reification.rationale: Nationalists backed protected national industry and did not hold a Marxian critique of markets; inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Burgher nationalists demanded press and assembly freedom as real rights in 1848, and did not call them hollow; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The 1848 constitution sought basic rights and rule through law, and the Rechtsstaat was central to the liberal national movement.

racial-franchise.rationale: The movement defined the nation by language and culture, and the Frankfurt constitution gave civic rights to all Germans, though later strands favoured descent; inferred.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic for the movement and not inferable from its principles; adherents neither favour nor oppose it.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; the Frankfurt Parliament sat in public but there is no doctrine on records of decisions.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Bismarck's Kulturkampf introduced compulsory civil marriage, and the national movement was not built on religious marriage rules; inferred.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Arndt and Jahn were hostile to Jews, but boycotts of shops were not a plank of the national movement; a typical adherent is inferred to disagree.

citizens-assembly.rationale: The 1848 movement sought an elected national parliament, so decisions by representatives were its model; disagreement is inferred, as lot-based assemblies were never discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The national movement was largely indifferent to doctrinal questions, and Protestant and Catholic adherents differed on how far to modernise religion.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The national movement was a constitutional and cultural project with no doctrine on wealth concentration; inferred from its support for protecting national industry, so the answer is neutral.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the Imperial German army's conservative, militarist culture and the criminalisation of homosexual acts under Paragraph 175; the movement never addressed the question.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred from nationalists such as Fichte and Arndt grounding the nation in Christian or religious moral renewal; state-imposed atheism is far from their program.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Nationalists wanted a strong, orderly state with a standing army and police, so abolishing police and prisons is inferred as strongly rejected.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the aim of a unified nation-state under one national government, which sat uneasily with granting communities veto-style shared executive power.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred only weakly: the movement said little about poor relief, and both church charity and later state insurance fit conservative nationalist views.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits are not a topic the movement addressed; its constitutional wing wanted a parliament and its authoritarian wing a hereditary monarchy, so adherents split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the Imperial and Wilhelmine strand's authoritarian, hierarchical view of politics, which would not accept revocable per-issue delegation.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic: the movement predates the concept, and nothing in its principles bears on extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the movement's Protestant and Catholic traditionalism, in which clerical offices were male; the issue was not raised.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the patriarchal family model of nineteenth-century Germany, including the 1900 Civil Code, which nationalists did not challenge.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the heredity-based, ethnic-cultural definition of the nation and the hostility to foreign groups.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred; the movement is a constitutional and cultural project that prefers protecting national industry, not price controls.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from List's emphasis on property, industry and national economic protection.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Jahn's Turnvereine and the Lutzow Free Corps organised drilled youth for national strength and liberation.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement did not address nuclear weapons and adherents' inferred views split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from the Pan-German insistence on German sovereignty and military strength.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Anachronistic and not addressed; adherents would be split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred; List favoured state direction of development but nationalists had no stated view on rentier income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from Jahn's Lutzow Free Corps and the movement's militarism.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Fichte presents the Germans as an original people whose language and spirit continue from the earliest times.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred; the movement's ethnic, Volkstum and traditional views of men and women are opposed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred; the movement's traditional view treats women's roles as fixed.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the cult of those who fell in the wars of liberation.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Inferred; the movement was cultural and political, not framed as a spiritual war.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Pan-Germanism wanted all Germans united in one Greater German state, not a homeland serving a diaspora.

culture-before-state.rationale: Fichte's Addresses call for national education and cultural unity as the basis of a future German state.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred; the movement kept traditional religious language.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred; the movement kept traditional religious authority.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Arndt's hostility to Jews and Poles implies keeping German economic life in German hands.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Pan-German demands for a Greater Germany would merge German-inhabited regions into one unit.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred: the movement stressed duty to the nation and a strong state, and the Wilhelmine strand was hostile to independent labour organisation.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred: the movement was nationalist, monarchist and anti-socialist, and rejected class rule by workers.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred: List favoured state direction of development and railways, but the movement had no doctrine on local services.

second-chamber.rationale: The 1848 Frankfurt constitution had a Volkshaus and a Staatenhaus, and the Imperial Bundesrat later played this role, so a second chamber suited the movement.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred: the movement favoured national economic unity under protection and private property, not communal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred: the movement sought a unified national state, and confederal local rule is the opposite of its centralising aim.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: the movement valued the family and Volk, and a family wage fits its traditionalist social outlook.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: The movement never addressed drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: The movement never addressed ageing research.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred: the authoritarian Imperial strand favoured state oversight, and a state-centred nation is hostile to untraceable money.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred: the movement's authoritarian Imperial form favoured state control of the press and associations.

person-over-state.rationale: Fichte and the movement stressed duty to the nation over the individual, so the person is not placed above the state.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Fichte invoked spiritual and religious motifs, but the movement was split between Protestant, Catholic and secular nationalists.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: the movement wanted a unified state and the Kaiserreich kept the member states' powers under imperial law.

gm-crops.rationale: The movement never addressed agricultural biotechnology.

dense-cities.rationale: The movement never addressed urban form, though it valued agrarian Volkstum.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Arndt and Jahn defined the nation by descent and Volkstum, and held that Germans had interests distinct from foreign peoples.

racial-pride.rationale: Pride in the German Volk and its ancestry was central to Arndt, Jahn and Fichte.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The Pan-German strand and the Imperial state were expansionist and militarist, so adherents rejected a strictly defensive limit.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Fichte's Addresses define the German nation by common language and culture, and the movement sought one state for all German speakers.

communal-electorates.rationale: The movement sought one national community and the Frankfurt Parliament proclaimed equal civil rights regardless of confession, while Imperial nationalists fought the Catholic Church in the Kulturkampf, so separate electorates cut against national unity.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Arndt, Jahn and Fichte were shaped by Napoleonic occupation and wariness of foreign influence, and later Pan-Germans spoke of encirclement, but the claim was not a standing doctrine of the 1848 strand.

free-public-college.rationale: The movement valued national education and Fichte called for state schooling, but tuition was not an issue for it; inferred and split.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pollution taxes are anachronistic; a movement favouring state direction of development and protection of national industry is inferred to oppose such taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Romantic nationalists framed the nation as a bond of ancestors and descendants, which loosely suggests a duty to later generations, but ecology was not at issue; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The movement assigned women to the home and the nation's maternal role and did not weigh gendered values in public life; inferred from the era's nationalist gender norms.

arms-reduction.rationale: The national movement from Jahn's Turnverein and the Lutzow Free Corps to Wilhelmine Pan-Germanism prized strong armed forces and military preparedness, so cutting them to a minimum would be rejected.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Bismarckian and Pan-German nationalism practised secret alliances and cabinet diplomacy, while the liberal 1848 strand was more open; the majority view is inferred to reject open diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: Friedrich List's national economics favoured state direction and protective tariffs to build the nation's economy, which suggests support for capital controls, but he addressed trade rather than capital flows; inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament sought a unified state with a national army under the central government, and Prussian-led Imperial Germany kept the military under state control; inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nationalists such as Arndt, Jahn and the Pan-Germans glorified national war and duty to the nation, so refusing to fight would be rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Imperial German nationalism backed hierarchy, and nationalists such as Jahn favoured social order; collective bargaining was not a nationalist demand, so mild disagreement is inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credits were unknown to the 1806-1871 movement; no clear inference from its principles.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The movement did not address fiscal rules; List favoured state direction of development, but this does not settle borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: German nationalism put the interests of the nation first, as in List's national economy, rather than rebalancing the world economy for other countries; inferred.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement sought a constitutional monarchy or authoritarian empire built on existing state institutions rather than their destruction.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: German nationalists favoured protection and state direction of national development, not open experiments; inferred from List.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Environmental accounting is anachronistic for the movement; inferred as neutral.

sacred-nation.rationale: Fichte's Addresses present the nation as an eternal community to which individuals owe duty and through which they gain lasting significance.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Student debt is anachronistic and not addressed by the movement; inferred as neutral.

internal-colonialism.rationale: German nationalists treated the nation as one economic and cultural unit, so internal colonialism would be rejected as divisive; inferred from List.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Nationalists such as Arndt and Fichte stressed distinct national character over universal human nature, while the 1848 liberals backed basic rights; split.

public-service-media.rationale: The movement had no public media policy; inferred as neutral.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Fichte-style nationalism tied the nation to German culture and Imperial nationalism fought Catholicism in the Kulturkampf and Los von Rom, so a single shared religious truth is inferred to be unwelcome.

farm-price-support.rationale: Nationalists backed protecting national production as List did and the Imperial state later protected agriculture; farm price support is inferred from this.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic for the era; inferred from the movement's strong support for national armed forces and military power.

workers-own-party.rationale: The movement sought unity of the whole nation across classes, as at Frankfurt, so a separate class party is inferred to cut against it.

ban-fgm.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's constitutional, rights-based aims at Frankfurt, though it never addressed the issue.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Frankfurt's basic rights said little about women and conservative nationalists upheld traditional roles, so adherents are inferred to be split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: The Sprachnation idea defined the nation by its common language, so one language across regions is inferred, though dialect names were not discussed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Imperial and Prussian nationalism favoured a strong state administration over private litigation; anachronistic and inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament wanted a constitution and elected assembly under an emperor, with no formal role for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement prized economic development and national power over limits on them, so this is inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Imperial nationalism was authoritarian and order-minded, so fixed severe sentences are inferred; not directly addressed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Fichte and Arndt stressed language as the mark of the nation, so a required national language is inferred to be welcome.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Trade unions were not a concern of the national movement and Imperial Germany both repressed and later tolerated them; inferred as neutral.

voter-id.rationale: The movement tied political rights to membership of the nation, so citizenship-based voting is inferred; ID checks themselves were never discussed.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The 1848 liberal strand wanted religious freedom within a unified state, but the later Bismarckian state fought the Catholic church; inferred as mildly in favor.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament was elected and sought a constitution, while Wilhelmine nationalism accepted an authoritarian monarchy, so the strand is split.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conservative, patriarchal moral outlook, as in Jahn's disciplined gymnastics movement; the sources do not discuss it.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement's strong-state and militarist strand might accept it but its liberal strand would not.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The movement favored protection of national industry and had no program for cash welfare; inferred as disagree.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament was elected by men only and nationalists of the period treated politics as a male sphere.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reverence for traditional family, church and national culture; it never framed religion as oppressive.

race-social-construct.rationale: Fichte defined the nation by language and culture and the Pan-German strand grew more racial, so a scientific-basis view is inferred over social construction.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: State agencies for gender equality are anachronistic and clash with the movement's traditional gender roles; inferred.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The national movement had no doctrine on first-claim property; it was a constitutional and cultural project, inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic for a movement of 1806-1871; its sovereignty-minded nationalism suggests resistance to outside judgment, inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The movement's Romantic and liberal leaders tied the nation to language and culture, not to literal scripture; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Anachronistic; the all-male Frankfurt Parliament shows women's participation was not a demand, inferred.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement favoured national industry and a market with tariffs, not planned economies, inferred.

indirect-election.rationale: The Frankfurt Parliament's constitution provided a directly elected lower house, so direct election is inferred as the preference.

national-church-status.rationale: Adherents were split between Protestants and Catholics and the movement defined the nation by language rather than church; inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The movement aimed at a unified centralised nation-state and gave little thought to minority regions; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Pan-German claims followed language and descent rather than popular votes, while some nationalists accepted plebiscites; adherents are split, inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic; the movement predates and has no doctrine on decolonisation, inferred.

simple-living.rationale: The movement valued national character and physical discipline, as in Jahn's gymnastics, but set no rule of simple living; inferred.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: The movement had no indigenous-settlement question in this sense; inferred as neutral.

equal-conscription.rationale: Jahn and Arndt called for a male citizen army, and the movement never extended duty to women; inferred.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Arndt and Jahn tied the Volk to the German land and Volkstum, and Fichte treated the nation as a community of duty; the sources record this, though not as a land-protection doctrine.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the Frankfurt Parliament's basic rights and the constitutional-state aims of the movement leave no room for killing without trial.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Imperial and Pan-German orientation toward continental power and colonies rather than Asian partnership.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Pan-Germanism sought to unite Germans living outside the state, including in Austria-Hungary, in a Greater Germany.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred: the movement backed private property and national industry, not common ownership of resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred: Fichte stressed duty to the nation and national education over individual claims against the community.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Taxation on consumption was not a nationalist issue; Zollverein-era tariffs were an indirect tax but no stance is documented.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Welfare targeting was not an issue for the movement; no position is documented and none can be inferred.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred: the 1848 aim was a parliament and later the Wilhelmine state worked through institutions, not a leader bypassing parties.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from List's case for state protection and direction of national industry, which means favouring some firms.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from Imperial nationalism's Kulturkampf against the Catholic political milieu and its aim of national cultural unity.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: nationalists celebrated Volkstum and German tradition while pushing railways and industrial development, as List did.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the conservative, patriarchal social order of the movement's burgher and monarchist supporters.

national-resource-control.rationale: List's national-economy doctrine treated the nation as the economic unit to be developed and protected from foreign domination.

missingStatements.text: The people of a nation should be united in a single state with a written constitution rather than divided among many princely states.
missingStatements.rationale: Unifying the many German states under one constitution was the Frankfurt Parliament's stated task.

missingStatements.text: A nation's language and culture, not its current borders, define who belongs to it.
missingStatements.rationale: Fichte defined the German nation by language and culture, and the Sprachnation concept guided later claims.

notes: Strands differ: the 1848 liberal wing wanted a parliamentary monarchy and basic rights, while the Bismarckian and Pan-German wings were authoritarian and expansionist. Answers on economics and social policy are inferences.
